old: Impersonal *se* is useful when the person performing an action is not specified. Passive-like *se* constructions describe rules, services and general workplace processes without focusing on an individual agent.
new: The pronoun *se* lets you leave out who does the action, which is useful for rules, services and general workplace processes. With a noun, the verb agrees with it (passive *se*): *se busca una persona*, *se buscan personas*. With no noun, the verb stays singular (impersonal *se*): *se trabaja mucho aquí*.
why: All four examples were passive se; the screen called them impersonal and showed no true impersonal. Text rewritten and an impersonal example added.

old: Use impersonal *se* when the agent is general or unknown. With plural nouns, the verb agrees with the noun in passive-like *se* constructions.
new: Use *se* when the agent is general or unknown. Singular noun, singular verb (*se organiza una reunión*); plural noun, plural verb (*se organizan reuniones*); no noun, singular verb (*se trabaja*).

old: Workplace problems can be explained by linking a cause to a consequence. *Porque*, *debido a*, *por eso*, *por lo tanto* and *así que* show why something happened and what followed.
new: You know *porque* from A1, *por eso* from A2 Unit 5 and *así que* from B1 Unit 1. New here is the formal *debido a* (“because of”), which you can use to explain a workplace problem: it links a cause to a consequence.
why: Presented known connectors as new and used por lo tanto (B2 consequence-markers). Recap added, por lo tanto removed.

old: *Por lo tanto* reads like a line from a written report; *por eso* is what you'd actually say to a colleague. Both introduce a consequence — picking between them signals how formal the moment is, not the logic.
new: *Debido a* and *a raíz de* mean “because of” and take a noun (*debido a un error*), never a verb; *porque* takes a verb (*porque había un error*). *Por eso* and *así que* introduce the consequence.
why: Tip removed por lo tanto (B2) and states the noun/verb rule of the taught connector; adds a raíz de named in the skill title.
"análisis" is in no vocabulary list; first use is in this lesson (grammar example, ex04).
